title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 'loop equation' manuscript, the continuation of the Longue Marche. Grothendieck is studying Galois-type automorphism groups of a profinite modular or mapping-class group, apparently the profinite completion of SL2(Z) ≅ Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6. Here rho_0 and sigma_0 are the standard torsion generators (orders 6 and 4), and L_rho ≅ Z/6, L_sigma ≅ Z/4 are the cyclic subgroups they generate. M is a large automorphism group mapping to Gamma_0 := Gamma~_{Q,*}, a (completed, pointed) Galois-type group. M^natural is a subgroup cut out by the conditions on the previous pages.

He has built M^natural_{rho0,sigma0}. It consists of triples (u_rho, u_sigma, u) with u in M^natural, and u_rho, u_sigma in the normalizers N^natural_{rho0}, N^natural_{sigma0}. These normalizers consist of automorphisms sending rho to rho^{eps_3(u)} and sigma to sigma^{eps_2(u)}, with all three having the same image in Gamma_0^natural. A fibre product over Gamma_0 rigidifies the 'up to conjugacy' data.

(120) Projection to the u-component gives a surjection onto M^natural. Its kernel is SZ_{rho0} × SZ_{sigma0}. Assuming the relevant centralizers of the torsion elements are just the cyclic groups L_rho, L_sigma, this kernel is ≅ Z/6 × Z/4: a 'tiny' group.

Goal: cut out a still smaller subgroup that is an extension of M^natural by mu. Here mu is presumably mu_2 = {±1}, the common centre L_rho ∩ L_sigma.

(121) He notes that M^natural_{rho0,sigma0} sits inside the fibre product N_{rho0} ×_{Gamma0} N_{sigma0} ×_{Gamma0} M for the full group. That fibre product is the group M_{rho,sigma} of pp. 625 ff., the case G_0^{natural'} = G_0^+. He recalls that inside it he had defined a subgroup (called M^natural_{rho,sigma} on p. 626'). He now renames it M^{?!}_{rho0,sigma0}. The next page defines it as N^?_rho ×_{Gamma0} Z^!_{sigma0} ×_{Gamma0} M, using centralizers intersected with M^!. The intended group is then the intersection of the two.

Purpose: canonically rigidify the extension of the 'Teichmüller/GT-type' group by the finite stabilizer data, reducing the finite kernel from Z/6×Z/4 to mu_2. This is bookkeeping for the action on the profinite modular tower.
errors: Equation numbers are (120) and (121) on the image, not (170)/(171); this is consistent with (119) on the previous page and (122) on the next.

The isomorphism SZ ≅ L_rho, L_sigma tacitly uses that the centralizer of a torsion element in the profinite completion of SL2(Z) (or the relevant group) is the finite cyclic group it generates. This is true for profinite amalgamated products (Herfort–Ribes type results), but it is not justified on this page.
The page is a draft: the first attempt at the definition is struck out, and the reduction to an extension by mu is announced but not completed here.

ideas.what: Rigidifying a group of outer-type automorphisms via a fibre product over Gamma_0 with normalizers of the torsion subgroups, giving a finite kernel Z/6×Z/4
ideas.modern_name: rigidification / stabilizer extensions in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory (action on profinite SL2(Z), torsion elements of orders 4 and 6)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld 1990; Ihara; Lochak–Schneps; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (structure of GT and its torsion)
ideas.where_published: Not published; Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the Teichmüller tower

ideas.what: Centralizer of a torsion element in the profinite modular group equals the cyclic group it generates
ideas.modern_name: centralizers of finite subgroups in profinite free products with amalgamation

ideas.what: Cutting the finite kernel down to mu_2 = centre, to get an extension of M^natural by mu
ideas.modern_name: central extension by ±1 (SL2 vs PSL2 lifting)

deep.surprise_reason: Technical bookkeeping inside the long unpublished study of GT-type groups acting on profinite SL2(Z). It is consistent with later GT literature, and nothing on this page alone goes beyond it.
transcription_corrections: Gamma_0 is defined as Gamma~_{Q,*} (tilde over Gamma, subscript Q,*).
'N/où[?]' should probably read 'NB : ce dernier produit fibré…'.
M^natural in the first line of (120) is written M^natural_{rho0,sigma0} with an arrow labelled 'pr'.
